verbalization: The visible evidence suggests a complex, multi-step relationship between (-) Carveol and Solute carrier organic anion transporter family member 1B3. (-) Carveol is directly linked to Sn1-specific diacylglycerol lipase beta, which is a target of a compound called (S)-2-(2-oxo-1,2-dihydroquinoline-4-carboxamido)succinic acid. This compound, in turn, targets Solute carrier organic anion transporter family member 1B3. The integration of these pathways implies that (-) Carveol may influence the activity of diacylglycerol lipase beta, which could then modulate the function of Solute carrier organic anion transporter family member 1B3. The mechanism is likely mediated through the regulation of diacylglycerol levels, which can affect the transport activity of the latter transporter. The evidence supports a role for (-) Carveol in influencing the downstream effects of diacylglycerol lipase beta, thereby impacting the transport function of Solute carrier organic anion transporter family member 1B3.
